quotes.text: The DevOps promise didn't fail because the idea was wrong. It failed because it scaled wrong.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's central thesis in two sentences.

quotes.text: A golden path is an opinionated pre-built workflow that handles the 80% of use cases that are actually common, not all use cases, not every possible variation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Precise, quotable definition of a golden path.

quotes.text: Self-service does not mean uncontrolled. It means controlled by policy and not by process. A policy is code. It runs automatically. It blocks the wrong action before it happens.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains how self-service and governance can coexist.

quotes.text: Adoption is the only metric that actually matters. If teams aren't using your platform, it's not because they're incompetent.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes platform success around voluntary adoption.

quotes.text: You can't rely on agents to understand what they shouldn't do. You have to make it impossible for them to do it. The solution is to embed governance at the API level.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear recommendation for governing AI agents on infrastructure.

takeaways: The DevOps tax is the hidden cost of making every team run its own infrastructure at scale, paid in cognitive load, tool sprawl, shadow IT and burnout.
Platform engineering inverts the model: a platform team treats infrastructure as a product and offers golden paths built on infrastructure as code and policy as code.
Success is measured by voluntary adoption, developer experience, DORA metrics and reduced cognitive load, and the same embedded governance lets AI agents such as Copilot operate safely.
hook: Developers are drowning in Kubernetes, pipelines and compliance checklists instead of shipping features. This episode is for engineering leaders and platform teams who want to understand the DevOps tax and replace it with platform engineering, from golden paths and policy as code to Team Topologies, measurement and AI-ready governance.
